subject: DPA: prohibiting ML derivative use / subprocessors & execution
messages:
From: Elena Morales <elena.morales@novidhealth.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procure@novidhealth.com>, Novid Legal <legal@novidhealth.com>
Date: 2027-03-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: DPA request: restrictions on ML/model improvement use + subprocessors

Hi Mateo,

Thanks for the quick demo last week — excited about the performance gains Redwood showed on our throughput tests. Before we proceed to POC, legal and procurement have asked us to get a DPA in place that explicitly prohibits using Novid customer data for model training or model improvement (we need a firm carve-out). They also want a current list of subprocessors and confirmation of cross-border transfer mechanics (we're EU-based operations for some customers).

Attached is a short summary of Novid's standard DPA asks and a redline template from our counsel. Key asks:
- Explicit non-training clause: "Customer Data will not be used for model training, tuning, or derivative model development."
- Definition of "Model Improvement" clarified (we provide suggested language).
- Subprocessor transparency and 30-day notice for new subprocessors.
- Data residency/transfer mechanism (SCCs or explicit contract clause).

Can you confirm Redwood's ability to accept that language or propose alternate wording? Procurement will need an executed agreement via DocuSign.

Regards,
Elena
Elena Morales
Head of Legal Ops, Novid Health
[Attachment: Novid_DPA_request.pdf (PDF)]

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena.morales@novidhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-19T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: DPA request: restrictions on ML/model improvement use + subprocessors

Elena — thanks for the note and the file. Appreciate the clarity.

Short answer: we can get you a DPA that meets Novid's needs, but we have a couple of follow-ups so we align precisely on definitions and mechanism. Next steps I propose:
1) Our legal team will propose targeted redlines to your template (attached) that include explicit carve-out language around "no model training or derivation."
2) We'll include our current subprocessors matrix and an operational process for 30-day notice on additions.
3) For transfers, Redwood prefers SCCs + logging of cross-border flows; if Novid requires a different mechanism we can escalate.

I've attached Redwood's initial redlines (Redwood_DPA_redlines_v2.docx). Marissa / Naomi — can you review the Novid asks and the redlines and flag any non-starters? Karthik, FYI on the POC timeline — procurement wants signed before we provision the sandbox.

Best,
Mateo
Mateo Alvarez
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Redwood_DPA_redlines_v2.docx (DOCX)]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-25T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: DPA request: redline summary & recommended language

On Thu, Mar 25, 2027 at 10:05 AM PDT, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com> wrote:

Team — I reviewed Novid's template and Mateo's initial redlines. Summary and suggested language below (I'll incorporate the exact text into the attached redline):

High-level position: we will accept an explicit prohibition on using Customer Data for training/derivative modelling provided we include mutually-agreed definitions and carve-outs for necessary operational telemetry and model evaluation on pseudonymized metrics. We do not accept open-ended restrictions that prevent us from diagnosing service issues.

Recommended changes (key bullets):
- "Customer Data" scope: keep Novid's proposed scope but ensure that aggregated/anonymized telemetry that cannot be re-associated with an identifiable Novid end-user is out of scope for "Customer Data" used for internal product analytics.
- "Model Improvement" definition: propose the following definition to avoid ambiguity — "Model Improvement" means modification to model parameters that results in an updated deployed model; excludes ephemeral prompt-level context used for a single request and operational performance metrics that are aggregated and not re-identifiable.
- Absolute ban language: accept a prohibition on training on Customer Data and derivative model development using Customer Data. Add language that allows Redwood to use de-identified, aggregated performance metrics and synthetic data not traceable to Customer Data.
- Subprocessors: provide current matrix (attached). Add 30-day notice for additions and right to object for critical subprocessors; objections trigger escalation and alternatives (SaaS self-hosting or dedicated capacity).
- Transfers: default to SCCs for EU transfers, plus logging of transfer events and customer's right to require regional-only deployment for regulated datasets (Redwood Dedicated/Private offering).

Open questions for Novid:
1) Are you comfortable with the proposed definition of "Model Improvement"?
2) For telemetry, can you accept the anonymization carve-out described above?
3) Procurement: do you require DocuSign for signature or AdobeSign?

I've attached a clean subprocessors matrix and will inline final redline once we settle the definition.

Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: subprocessors_matrix.xlsx (XLSX)]

From: Elena Morales <elena.morales@novidhealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procure@novidhealth.com>, Novid Legal <legal@novidhealth.com>
Date: 2027-03-29T14:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: DPA request: clarifications on definitions and execution route

Thanks Marissa — that helps. A few follow-ups from Novid Legal:

1) Model Improvement definition: we like the direction, but Novid needs a tighter restriction on "ephemeral prompt-level" data — specifically, Novid wants an explicit statement that prompts and completions stored longer than 30 days may not be used for model training. Can Redwood accept a 30-day retention ceiling for any customer prompt/completion content that could be considered part of Customer Data?

2) Telemetry carve-out: Novid is willing to accept aggregated metrics but requests an explicit prohibition on any attempt to re-identify or deanonymize. Include a covenant to not attempt deanonymization.

3) Execution: Procurement confirmed DocuSign only (AdobeSign is blocked by their procurement stack). Can you route the final redline to DocuSign?

If we can get agreement on the 30-day retention ceiling for prompt-level content and the anti-deanonymization covenant, procurement is ready to sign.

Best,
Elena
[Inline: Novid Legal comments]

[No attachment on this message]

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena.morales@novidhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Procurement <procure@novidhealth.com>
Date: 2027-04-02T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: DPA request: final redline and DocuSign execution

Elena — thanks for the clear asks. We reviewed with privacy and product. Final positions below and next steps:

- 30-day retention ceiling: Redwood cannot commit to a blanket 30-day retention ceiling for all prompt/completion content in hosted deployments because debugging and safety pipelines sometimes require short-term retention beyond 30 days. Instead we propose: default 30-day retention for prompt/completion content used in hosted Redwood API; exceptions allowed for specific debugging incidents with documented change control and customer notification. For regulated customers Novid can choose Dedicated/Private deployment where we can meet regional retention controls.

- Anti-deanonymization covenant: accepted in full. We'll add language that forbids attempts to re-identify or deanonymize Customer Data.

- Execution: DocuSign is fine. I've routed the agreed redline into DocuSign; procurement should see a signing request at the link below. I attached the executed DPA placeholder (we will upload the final executed PDF post-signature).

DocuSign link: https://docu-sign.example.com/r/abc123-exec-novid

Please confirm if Novid is happy to proceed with the proposed retention exception language or if you require dedicated/private deployment to proceed.

Thanks — Mateo
Mateo Alvarez
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: executed_DPA_Novid_Redwood.pdf (PDF) — executed copy will be uploaded after DocuSign completion]
